title: Multi-Host Sharing of a Single-Function NVMe Device in a PCIe Cluster
problem: NVMe-oF using RDMA introduces extra latency by requiring software on the critical path for distributed block-level storage access. There is a need to share NVMe devices across multiple hosts in a cluster without this latency overhead.
motivation: Distributed cluster applications including machine learning, databases, and HPC workloads require fast shared storage access without RDMA-induced latency penalties.
method: The authors develop a distributed NVMe driver that leverages PCIe shared memory capabilities to disaggregate NVMe controllers at the I/O queue level. This enables multiple remote hosts to access the same NVMe device in parallel without RDMA, and achieves performance comparable to local NVMe access.
key_novelty: Using PCIe shared memory to disaggregate NVMe controllers at the I/O queue level, enabling direct parallel access from remote hosts without RDMA.
contributions: Distributed NVMe driver for PCIe clusters enabling multi-host device sharing
I/O queue-level disaggregation of NVMe controllers for parallel remote access
PCIe-based alternative to RDMA with reduced network latency
Demonstration of near-local-access performance without RDMA software overhead

metrics.other: comparable to local NVMe access performance
